questions.q: A team wants to know the instant a nightly pipeline fails, rather than discovering it the next morning. What's the correct feature?
options: A OneLake data access role on the pipeline
An alert tied to the pipeline's run status
A deployment pipeline stage gate
Promoting the pipeline to a new workspace
questions.explain: Alerts (Fabric Lesson 53) push a notification the moment a run fails — deployment pipelines control code promotion, not failure notification.

questions.q: A team wants Fabric notebook changes tested in a Test workspace before reaching Production, with a record of who approved the change. What combination answers this?
options: The Monitoring Hub alone
A sensitivity label on the notebook
Git integration for the version trail, plus deployment pipelines for the promotion gate
Row-level security on the notebook
questions.explain: Git integration (Fabric Lesson 15) gives the change history and approval trail; deployment pipelines (Fabric Lesson 45, Git/CI-CD Lesson 22) give the Dev/Test/Prod gate.

questions.q: What does the Monitoring Hub actually show?
options: A promotion gate between Dev, Test, and Prod
The Git commit history for a notebook
Which workspace role each user holds
A live, cross-item view of what ran recently and whether it succeeded
questions.explain: The Monitoring Hub (Fabric Lesson 16) is a run-history and status view, not a permissions tool or a promotion mechanism.

questions.q: A scenario describes rolling out a pipeline change to production gradually, with the ability to revert quickly if something goes wrong. What pattern does this describe?
options: Blue-green or canary deployment
A sensitivity label
Row-level security
The Monitoring Hub
questions.explain: Blue-green and canary deployment (Fabric Lesson 65) are gradual-rollout-with-fast-rollback patterns — a deployment concern, not a monitoring one.

questions.q: Why is observability (logs, metrics, traces) a distinct concern from the Monitoring Hub's run-status view?
options: Observability provides the detail needed to diagnose why a failure happened, beyond just knowing that it failed
Observability replaces the need for alerts entirely
Observability and the Monitoring Hub are exactly the same feature under two names
Observability only applies to deployment pipelines, never to pipeline runs
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 52 covers observability as the deeper diagnostic layer — the Monitoring Hub tells you something failed, observability helps explain why.

questions.q: What does Fabric's native deployment pipelines feature let you do?
options: Diagnose why a Spark job ran slowly
Filter which rows a user sees in a semantic model
Send an alert when a pipeline run fails
Promote workspace items through Dev, Test, and Prod stages inside Fabric's own UI
questions.explain: Deployment pipelines (Fabric Lesson 15) are Fabric's built-in Dev/Test/Prod promotion mechanism for workspace items.

questions.q: A scenario names 'deployment pipelines' as an option for a question about catching a pipeline failure quickly. Why is this the wrong answer?
options: Deployment pipelines are only available in the Monitoring Hub
Deployment pipelines don't exist in Fabric
Deployment pipelines control code/item promotion between environments — they don't monitor running pipelines for failures
Deployment pipelines are a synonym for alerts
questions.explain: This is the classic Domain 3 trap: a real feature from the wrong family (deployment) offered as the answer to a monitoring question.
